thm:p1.source:
\begin{theorem}[Strong consistency and Fisher information convergence]
\label{thm:p1}
Let $L=B$ denote Algorithm~\ref{alg:mixed-bures} with allocation
$\pi_B$, and $L=F$ denote Algorithm~\ref{alg:mixed-frobenius} with
allocation $\pi_F(c_{n_-(t)})$ on copy $t$.
Both rules use the adaptive measurement axes
$v_{n_-(t),k}$ defined in~\eqref{eq:qubit-householder}, with the
design estimate $c_{n_-(t)}$ from the corresponding algorithm.
Here $n_-(t)=N_{j-1}$
for $N_{j-1}<t\le N_j$, as defined in~\eqref{eq:batches}.
For either rule $L\in\{B,F\}$, every fixed interior truth, every
$\lambda>0$, and every batch sequence~\eqref{eq:batches}, the
implemented estimator satisfies almost surely
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p1limit}
 \begin{gathered}
 \widehat\theta_n\to\theta_0,\qquad c_n\to\theta_0,\qquad
 \mathcal I_{\xi_t}(\theta_0)\to\mathcal I_L^\star,\\
 \frac1n\sum_{t\le n}\mathcal I_{\xi_t}(\theta_0)\to\mathcal I_L^\star,
 \qquad \frac1n\sum_{t\le n}\mathcal I_{a_t}(\theta_0)\to\mathcal I_L^\star.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Both safeguards, \eqref{eq:bures-safeguard} and~\eqref{eq:qubitcontroller},
are eventually inactive almost surely.
\end{theorem}

thm:p2efficient.source:
\begin{theorem}[Estimation rates and asymptotic normality]
\label{thm:p2efficient}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:p2}, the estimators in
Algorithm~\ref{alg:phase-paired} satisfy the following conclusions
along $n=N_j$, $j\to\infty$.

\noindent\textup{(i) Estimation rates.}
The matrix least-squares estimator and its rank-one projection satisfy
$\|\widehat A_n-P_0\|_F=O_p(n^{-1/2})$ and
$\|\widehat P_n-P_0\|_F=O_p(n^{-1/2})$.

\noindent\textup{(ii) Asymptotic normality.} In any fixed
smooth pure-state chart $(\mathcal U,\varphi)$ as in
Definition~\ref{def:pure-chart}, with $P_0\in\mathcal U$, let
$\theta_0=\varphi(P_0)$ and let $H(\theta_0)$ be the matrix in
the parametrization $\Gamma(\theta)=\varphi^{-1}(\theta)$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:efficientchartCLT}
 n^{1/2}\{\varphi(\widehat P_n^{\rm eff})-\varphi(P_0)\}
 \Longrightarrow\mathcal N_{2d}(0,2H(\theta_0)^{-1}).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, $n^{1/2}(\widehat P_n^{\rm eff}-P_0)$ converges in
distribution to a centered Gaussian supported on the true tangent space,
with identity covariance in Frobenius-orthonormal tangent coordinates.
\end{theorem}

thm:oracle-risk.source:
\begin{theorem}[Adaptive Gill--Massar bound]\label{thm:oracle-risk}
For either model above, let $H=H(\theta_0)\succ0$ be the
SLD quantum Fisher information matrix and $W\succeq0$ a weight in the
same coordinates. For any sequence of policies $(\zeta_t)_{t\ge1}$ as above,
under the conditional-likelihood assumptions in
Appendix~\ref{app:oracle-main}, every finite-valued coordinate estimator $T_n$ locally unbiased
at $\theta_0$ and every $n\ge1$ satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:oracle-finite-risk}
 n\,\E_{\theta_0}\!\left[
 (T_n-\theta_0)^{\mathsf T}W(T_n-\theta_0)\right]
 \ge C_{\rm GM}(W,H),
\end{equation}
where $C_{\rm GM}$ is defined in~\eqref{eq:gm-weighted-bound}.
\end{theorem}
